title: Recipe 34 — Building Custom Graders (a grader is an instrument; measure it)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “The bundled graders stop where your domain starts. This is the authoring loop for the one you have to write yourself.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe and the starter it borrows are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — only the judge beat at the end needs it.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the harness a grader plugs into

beats.label: Type the starter the recipe points at
beats.cue: “starters/eval is the runnable starting point: a math agent, a labelled dev split, one deterministic grader.”

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Clean before we add an instrument, so anything that moves later is the grader's doing.”

beats.label: Compile the scorer — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the emitted shape, installs the deps, boots it: GREEN, gated on a registered dataset rather than a key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (3 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the eval dataset gate (this scratch dir vendors no dataset)

beats.label: Type the recipe's pure-function grader
beats.cue: “The whole contract: sample in, run result in, and out comes passed, score, rationale. Thirteen lines, no framework.”

beats.label: Make it discoverable
beats.cue: “One default export is what turns a function into a plugin — and the name here is the REGISTERED name, not the file name.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's graders.yaml entry
beats.cue: “type: registry, and grader: is the registered name. name: is only the label the report prints.”

groups.title: Beat 3 · an unmeasured instrument is a guess

beats.label: Write three human-adjudicated verdicts
beats.cue: “Strict JSONL: an id, the input, the agent output, and what a human says the verdict should be.”

beats.label: Meta-eval the grader
beats.cue: “Agreement 100%, kappa 1.000, score error zero — and the gate passes. That number is about the instrument, not the agent. Credential-free: nothing called a model.”

verify.note: discovers the plugin from ./.crewhaus/graders, replays 3 golden verdicts: agreement 100% (3/3), kappa 1.000, MAE 0.000, gate passed

beats.label: Card the instrument
beats.cue: “Deterministic — no timestamps, identity is the gradersHash. So a card diff in a PR is a real instrument change, never noise.”

verify.note: writes the rubric card: gradersHash, combine policy, one registry grader

beats.label: Read the card
beats.cue: “This is what you attach to the release PR: the measurement instrument, in writing.”

groups.title: Beat 4 · the recipe's own tests, verbatim

beats.label: Import the grader under test
beats.cue: “Two imports — the grader is an ordinary function, so it tests like one.”
beats.text:
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

import { startsWithDigit } from "../.crewhaus/graders/starts-with-digit/index.ts";

beats.label: Type the recipe's fixture tests
beats.cue: “Straight out of the recipe's Testing graders section: one case that must pass, one that must fail.”

beats.label: Run them
beats.cue: “Two pass, zero fail, seven milliseconds. Deterministic, fast, free — which is why you reach for a pure function whenever you can.”

verify.note: 2 pass, 0 fail, 3 expect() calls — the recipe's own fenced tests against the recipe's own fenced grader

groups.title: One more thing · when the grader needs a model

beats.label: Start a judge config
beats.cue: “Fuzzy quality needs a model in the loop — and the second rubric branch picks exactly one label instead of a 1-to-5 score.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's categorical rubric
beats.cue: “The label scores and the passing set are deliberately hidden from the judge — it picks a label, the config decides what that means.”

beats.label: Meta-eval it with no credentials
beats.cue: “Exit one, on purpose: it names the missing key, skips the judge, and refuses to report an agreement it never measured. Deterministic graders would have kept testing — this file has none.”
beats.command: env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN crewhaus graders test --graders live/graders-judge.yaml --golden live/golden-verdicts.jsonl

verify.note: REAL exit 1 — “skipped llm_judge "verdict" — no credentials visible …” then “no testable graders”. Scrubs explicitly because the Setup group sourced .env into this same shell

beats.label: Now with a key
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same file, same goldens — the judge actually runs, and its agreement with the humans is the number that matters.”

verify.note: judges at the rubric's declared passing set; needs visible judge credentials (the calibrate --apply overlay is deliberately NOT applied here)
